Senses.Explanation: The lantern is a concrete hall object that the records repeatedly make the subject of questions, answers, speech, movement, and comparison. A lantern is the visible light-holder that Chan records repeatedly turn into a public-stage object and impossible participant. The word occurs 1,681 times in 293 allowlisted texts. Dizang Guichen points to one; in another exchange an unnamed monk names the lantern as form and asks which is mind, and Longji Shaoxiu answers that the lantern is mind. Guishan Lingyou answers a question about the ancestral teacher's coming from the west by pointing to the lantern and saying, 'a very good lantern.' The same object becomes a stock participant beside the exposed pillar: Dongshan Xiaocong says it dozes while the pillar is alert; Feiyin Tongrong makes lanterns dance while pillars knit their brows; Huitang Zuxin puts the three gates atop a lantern; and Fachang Yu says the lantern exposes sealed-mouth sitters. These are attributed answers and personifications; the records continue to name the same lantern without supplying another referent.
